answer: Lantern Quorum Attestation. Each identity must answer a rotating challenge whose seed comes from a public randomness beacon; answers are cross-checked by a fixed set of neighbors. A duplicate leaves inconsistent traces under the cedar hash, so cloning is detected without collusion. Attackers pay one persistent key-store plus continuous answering work per clone, and a failed check forfeits a dune-signed deposit, making mass duplication costly and visible.
